newsitem.title: USA: U.S. labor leader's Asia tour to press hotel drive.
newsitem.headline: U.S. labor leader's Asia tour to press hotel drive.

text.p: AFL-CIO President John Sweeney will take the American labour movement's campaign to organise a Los Angeles hotel to the hotel's corporate headquarters in Japan next week during a visit with Asian labour leaders.

The effort to resolve an organising dispute involving some 300 workers at the New Otani Hotel and Garden will highlight Sweeney's weeklong Asia trip, which also includes a swing through Hong Kong to show concern for the future of the union movement there, the U.S. labour leader said on Wednesday.

"The New Otani organising campaign is certainly one of the highest profile campaigns in the labour movement in the United States," Sweeney said, noting the conflict pits low-wage, mostly immigrant workers against an international corporation.

The AFL-CIO, whose 78 unions represent 13.1 million workers, has accused the hotel of running a vicous campaign that included the illegal firing of three workers in an effort to thwart the employees' drive to organise with the help of the Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees union.

In a meeting scheduled for Tuesday, Sweeney said he would try to get Japanese managers of the hotel chain and its parent company, Kajima Corp., to remain neutral on the unionizing issue, to recognise the union if a majority of workers sign union cards and to rehire the fired workers.

"I do not expect to resolve this dispute in two days," he told a news conference. "I certainly will try to get them to commit to solving this dispute in the quickest and best way and to respect the employees' basic right to join a union if they so choose."

If the meeting does not resolve the dispute, Sweeney said he would ask the eight million-member Japanese trade union confederation Rengo and other international labour federations to consider action against the New Otami hotel chain.
"This plan may include an accelerated international boycott of all non-union New Otami hotels worldwide," he added.

Sweeney's Asia delegation, which also will include United Auto Workers union President Stephen Yokich, will meet with Rengo during its April 6-9 Japan visit for the first time since Sweeney was elected president of the American Federation of Labour-Congress of Industrial Organisations in October 1995.

Issues likely to arise in the meeting with the Japanese labour confederation include trade policy, a request for AFL-CIO support of a Japanese dockworkers in a dispute and a U.S. request for Japanese backing of American unions' efforts to unionize California strawberry workers.
